name: Mind Lab Pro
summary: The most comprehensively researched nootropic stack available to Australian buyers. Most ingredients are clinically dosed and peer-reviewed. Ships from the UK directly to Australia. Imported as a food supplement -- Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA) listing required only if therapeutic claims are made. Our #1 pick for the Australian market.
whatItIs: Mind Lab Pro is an 11-ingredient pre-formulated nootropic stack made by Opti-Nutra, a UK-based supplement company. It ships directly to Australia and is designed as a complete daily cognitive supplement covering memory, focus, mental energy, mood, and long-term brain health without caffeine or proprietary blends. In Australia it is imported and sold as a food supplement rather than a listed therapeutic good.
howItWorks: Mind Lab Pro works across six bio-pathways simultaneously. Citicoline and Phosphatidylserine support the cholinergic system and neuronal membrane integrity. Lion's Mane stimulates Nerve Growth Factor (NGF) for neuroplasticity. Bacopa Monnieri enhances synaptic communication for memory. Rhodiola Rosea and L-Tyrosine support dopamine/norepinephrine balance under stress. L-Theanine promotes alpha brain wave activity for calm focus. B-vitamins support homocysteine regulation and neurotransmitter synthesis.
whatToExpect: Within 30-60 minutes: mild calm focus from L-Theanine. Within 2-4 weeks: improved mental energy and reduced cognitive fatigue. At 8-12 weeks: measurable improvements in memory recall and learning speed. Ships to Australia in 3–6 working days from the brand's Australian depot, or 7–14 working days when shipped from the UK (per mindlabpro.com, checked 2026-09-29). Australian buyers pay in USD. Best results require 3+ months of consistent daily use.
cons: Premium price ($69/mo USD)
2 capsules per serving (2–4 per day suggested)
30-day money-back
Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA) listing required for therapeutic claims -- imported as food supplement

name: NooCube
summary: Strong formula anchored by Lutemax 2020 for Australian screen workers. Ships from the UK/EU to Australia as an imported food supplement. A$84.99 for a 30-serving bottle on noocube.com.au. Note: the noocube.com Trustpilot profile has no reviews yet -- verify independently before purchasing.
whatItIs: NooCube is a 12-ingredient nootropic stack made by Wolfson Brands. Its standout feature is Lutemax 2020 -- a patented lutein and zeaxanthin extract researched for reducing digital eye strain and blue-light-related cognitive fatigue. Available for international shipping to Australia, it is imported as a food supplement.
howItWorks: Lutemax 2020 filters high-energy blue light in the retina, reducing eye fatigue during screen use -- particularly relevant for Australian remote workers and office professionals. Choline from VitaCholine supports the cholinergic system; the current formula no longer contains Alpha-GPC or Huperzine A. L-Theanine provides calm focus. Bacopa Monnieri targets memory consolidation over weeks.
whatToExpect: Day one: mild calm focus from L-Theanine. Within 2-4 weeks: reduced eye fatigue and better end-of-day mental stamina. At 8 weeks: modest memory improvements from Bacopa. Delivery to Australia is quoted as within 10 business days (per noocube.com, checked 2026-09-29). Australian buyers should verify the subscription cancellation policy before purchasing since the noocube.com Trustpilot profile has no reviews yet.
cons: No reviews on the noocube.com Trustpilot profile (checked 2026-09-28)
Some ingredients underdosed
Subscription cancellation issues (BBB)
Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA) listing required for therapeutic claims -- imported as food supplement
notes: Bulk-purchase pricing changed June 2026: 5-month supply $194.99 USD (was 6-month for $180). AU buyers purchasing direct affected.

name: Performance Lab Mind
summary: A minimalist, ultra-clean nootropic formula using premium patented ingredients. Ships to Australia from the UK. Imported as a food supplement. Ideal for Australian buyers who prefer a transparent, simple formula over large proprietary stacks.
whatItIs: Performance Lab Mind is a streamlined 4-ingredient nootropic by Performance Lab, a UK-based supplement company. It ships directly to Australia and uses only NutriGenesis and licensed raw materials with full label transparency. In Australia it is classified as an imported food supplement -- no TGA therapeutic claims are made on the label.
howItWorks: Citicoline (Cognizin) boosts brain cell membrane synthesis and acetylcholine production for focus and memory. Phosphatidylserine (Sharp-PS Green) maintains neuronal membrane fluidity and supports cortisol regulation under stress. L-Tyrosine replenishes catecholamine neurotransmitters depleted by cognitive effort. Maritime Pine Bark provides antioxidants that support cerebral blood flow.
whatToExpect: Day one: mild cognitive sharpness and sustained attention. Within 2-4 weeks: improved stress resilience and working memory. At 8 weeks: measurable reduction in mental fatigue during extended cognitive tasks. Ships to Australia in 3–6 working days from the brand's Australian depot, or 7–14 working days when shipped from the UK (per performancelab.com, checked 2026-09-29). Only 2 capsules per serving -- excellent for Australian buyers looking for a low pill-burden daily stack.
cons: Fewer total ingredients
Pricey per capsule
Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA) listing required for therapeutic claims -- imported as food supplement

discontinued.note: Opti-Nutra merged Performance Lab Mind into Mind Lab Pro; the vendor URL now redirects to Mind Lab Pro.

name: Hunter Focus
summary: A high-dose premium nootropic stack available to Australian buyers shipping from the UK. Contains caffeine. Imported as a food supplement -- no Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA) therapeutic claims on the label. No affiliate commission available.
whatItIs: Hunter Focus is a premium nootropic stack from Hunter Life designed for high-performance professionals. It ships internationally to Australia and combines cognitive ingredients with adaptogens at full clinical doses. In Australia it is imported as a food supplement. Contains 100mg caffeine per serving.
howItWorks: Lion's Mane stimulates Nerve Growth Factor for long-term neuroplasticity. Ashwagandha (KSM-66) reduces cortisol and stress-induced cognitive impairment. Citicoline supports acetylcholine production for focus and memory. Caffeine and L-Theanine (2:1 ratio) work synergistically for alert, jitter-free energy.
whatToExpect: Within 30-60 minutes: clear, stimulated focus from the caffeine/L-Theanine stack. Within 2-4 weeks: improved stress resilience from Ashwagandha. At 8-12 weeks: long-term neuroplasticity benefits from Lion's Mane. Check the delivery estimate for Australia at checkout. At $90 USD/month, it is one of the pricier options for Australian buyers, but ingredient doses are among the highest in this review.
pros: Full clinical doses across all ingredients
cons: Contains caffeine
No affiliate commission
Very expensive ($90/mo USD)
Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA) listing required for therapeutic claims -- imported as food supplement

name: Alpha Brain
summary: The most commercially recognised nootropic brand available to Australian buyers. Backed by two clinical studies and NSF Certified for Sport. Imported as a food supplement -- Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA) listing required for therapeutic claims. Well suited for Australian athletes and mainstream shoppers.
whatItIs: Alpha Brain is Onnit's flagship nootropic, first released in 2011 and popularised through Joe Rogan's podcast. It is the most recognised nootropic brand in the English-speaking world, making it a familiar choice for Australian buyers. It is imported from the US to Australia as a food supplement. National Sanitation Foundation (NSF) Certified for Sport makes it suitable for Australian drug-tested athletes.
howItWorks: Alpha Brain uses three proprietary blends -- Onnit Flow Blend, Focus Blend, and Fuel Blend -- containing cholinergics (Alpha-GPC), adaptogens (Bacopa), and amino acids (Tyrosine, Theanine). Because doses are hidden in proprietary blends, individual ingredient doses cannot be verified against clinical thresholds. The two published studies (Onnit-funded, 2016 and 2021) tested the full formula and showed statistically significant improvements in verbal memory and executive function versus placebo.
whatToExpect: Day one: subtle focus improvement, particularly for users new to cholinergic supplements. Caffeine-free means no energy spike -- effects are gentle. At 4-6 weeks: most users report mild improvements in word retrieval and task focus. The 90-day money-back guarantee is one of the most generous in the category. Ships from the US to Australia -- check the delivery estimate for Australia at checkout.
cons: Proprietary blends hide doses
Subscription cancellation issues
Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA) listing required for therapeutic claims -- imported as food supplement

name: Qualia Mind
summary: 28 active ingredients -- the most comprehensive formula available to Australian buyers. Best for experienced Australian biohackers. Ships from the US to Australia. Note: Huperzine A may require Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA) oversight if sold with therapeutic claims. At $139 USD/month it is the most expensive option in this review.
whatItIs: Qualia Mind is a 28-ingredient nootropic stack developed by Neurohacker Collective, a San Diego-based company focused on systems biology and complex supplementation. It ships to Australia from the US and is designed for experienced supplement users. Imported as a food supplement in Australia -- Australian buyers should note that some ingredients (including Huperzine A) may attract TGA scrutiny if accompanied by therapeutic claims.
howItWorks: Qualia Mind covers more cognitive pathways than any competitor: cholinergics (Alpha-GPC, Huperzine A, Citicoline), adaptogens (Rhodiola, Bacopa), neuro-nutrients (DHA, PS), amino acid precursors (Tyrosine, Taurine, Theanine), B-vitamin complex, and novel ingredients (Uridine Monophosphate, Pyrroloquinoline Quinone). The theory is synergistic optimisation across all cognitive systems simultaneously.
whatToExpect: Acute effects day one: sustained attention, moderate energy boost from caffeine (90mg per serving). Within 2-4 weeks: improved mental endurance and working memory. At 8-12 weeks: cumulative adaptogen and memory benefits. International delivery is estimated at 15-22 days (per qualialife.com, checked 2026-09-29). 6 capsules per serving is a significant daily pill burden. Start with the recommended 7-day loading cycle (2 days off per week) to assess tolerance.
cons: $139/month USD
6 capsules per serving
Contains caffeine
Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA) listing required for therapeutic claims -- imported as food supplement

name: NatureBell Ginkgo + Ginseng
summary: NatureBell Ginkgo + Ginseng is the most affordable nootropic in this review at approximately AUD $8/month for a 5-month supply (300 capsules). Chinese-manufactured with US branding, available on Amazon.com.au with Prime shipping across Australia. Ginkgo Biloba at clinical dose (120mg) paired with Panax Ginseng. Best as a budget entry point for Australian buyers.
whatItIs: NatureBell is a US-registered supplement brand sourcing from Chinese manufacturers. Their Ginkgo + Ginseng formula delivers 120mg Ginkgo Biloba extract (50:1 concentration) at the full clinical dose, paired with Panax Ginseng. Available on Amazon.com.au with Prime shipping to all Australian states and territories. The 300-capsule bottle provides a 5-month supply at approximately AUD $40. Not Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA) registered — imported as a personal-use supplement via Amazon.
howItWorks: Ginkgo Biloba improves cerebral blood flow via vasodilation and platelet-activating factor (PAF) inhibition. Panax Ginseng contains ginsenosides that modulate NMDA receptor activity and support dopaminergic signalling. The Ginkgo-Ginseng pairing is one of the oldest TCM cognitive combinations.
whatToExpect: Weeks 1-2: mild improvement in mental alertness from Ginkgo blood flow effects. Weeks 4-8: cumulative memory benefits. Ginseng dose is well below clinical levels (10mg vs 200mg). Best used as a stack addition alongside a premium nootropic.
cons: Ginseng severely underdosed
Not TGA-registered
No third-party CoA published
Two-ingredient formula only

name: Blackmores Brain Active
summary: Blackmores Brain Active was a pharmacy-shelf cognitive supplement in Australia and is now discontinued. Our earlier copy cited AUST L 246877, which does not resolve on the Australian Register of Therapeutic Goods (ARTG). TGA's cancellation register lists ARTG entry 227270 for Blackmores Brain Active, cancelled 18 September 2014; we found no current ARTG entry (searched 2026-09-30). Bacopa Monnieri at clinical dose (300mg) is the ingredient that earns its trust score. Founded 1932 — the longest-tenured Australian supplement brand.
whatItIs: Blackmores is Australia's largest naturopathic supplement company, founded in 1932 by chiropractor Maurice Blackmore. Brain Active was one of their cognitive products. TGA's cancellation register lists its Australian Register of Therapeutic Goods (ARTG) entry, 227270, as cancelled on 18 September 2014, and we found no current ARTG entry (searched 2026-09-30). No DTC subscription model. Daily 1-capsule format reduces friction.
howItWorks: Bacopa Monnieri at 300mg (clinical dose, standardized to 50% bacosides) supports memory consolidation over 8-12 weeks of consistent use — the most-replicated memory ingredient in nootropics. Ginkgo Biloba supports cerebral blood flow but at 40mg is well below the 120mg clinical anchor. B5 and B12 act as cofactors for energy metabolism. The Bacopa is the workhorse; the rest are supporting cast.
whatToExpect: Acute: nothing dramatic. This is a long-onset memory-focused supplement. Weeks 4-8: subtle memory and attention improvements from Bacopa accumulation. Weeks 12+: cumulative effect peaks. Best used as a daily long-term cognitive supplement rather than an acute focus boost. Caffeine-free — no overlap with morning coffee.
pros: Lowest per-month price in the AU coverage (~AUD $35/mo)
Founded 1932 — strongest brand-trust footprint in Australian supplements
cons: Ginkgo dose (40mg) well below clinical anchor (120-240mg)
Iodine dose at 50% RDI — odd inclusion in a cognitive supplement
No L-theanine, no citicoline, no Lion's Mane
No DTC affiliate — must buy at retail (no online comparison-pricing leverage)
Slow-onset (8+ weeks) — not for acute focus

discontinued.note: No longer listed on blackmores.com.au or at Chemist Warehouse; Blackmores now sells Cognition Ultra / Omega Brain.

name: Performance Lab Caffeine 2
summary: A low-dose caffeine capsule from Performance Lab: 50mg natural caffeine with 100mg L-theanine (a 2:1 ratio), 250mg L-tyrosine and four B-vitamins, with every dose on the label. Australian orders ship from the brand's Australian or UK depot (per performancelab.com's shipping page, checked 2026-10-05); it is imported as a food supplement, not a listed medicine.
whatItIs: Performance Lab Caffeine 2 is a stimulant capsule sold through performancelab.com. Each vegan pullulan capsule holds 50mg natural caffeine from Coffea robusta seeds, 100mg L-theanine, 250mg L-tyrosine and NutriGenesis vitamins B2, B6, folate and B12; a bottle holds 30 capsules. The label suggests 1-2 capsules on an empty stomach, up to a maximum of 5 capsules (250mg caffeine) a day. We found no entry for it on the Australian Register of Therapeutic Goods (ARTG) when we searched on 2026-10-05, so it reaches Australian buyers as an imported food supplement rather than a listed medicine.
howItWorks: Caffeine blocks adenosine receptors, which dulls fatigue signals and raises alertness. L-theanine, an amino acid found in tea, is added at a 2:1 ratio to caffeine; Performance Lab cites human trials of theanine-plus-caffeine combinations for this pairing, but Caffeine 2 itself has not been tested in a published trial. L-tyrosine is a building block of dopamine and noradrenaline, and the vendor includes it to support the neurotransmitters that caffeine draws on. The four B-vitamins (B2, B6, folate, B12) supply 38-83% of the US Daily Value per capsule.
whatToExpect: Performance Lab says Caffeine 2 starts working in around 15-30 minutes. One capsule gives 50mg caffeine; two capsules (100mg caffeine, 200mg L-theanine, 500mg L-tyrosine) bring all three actives into the ranges used in our dosing audit. Count it toward your daily caffeine intake. Orders to Australia ship from the brand's Australian depot in 3-6 working days or from its UK depot in 7-14 working days, depending on destination (per performancelab.com's shipping page, checked 2026-10-05). We saw only US-dollar prices ($44 one-time) when we checked.
pros: Every dose disclosed on the label, no proprietary blend
Ships from an Australian depot (3-6 working days) or the UK (7-14)
50mg caffeine per capsule lets you adjust intake in small steps (label maximum 5 a day)
cons: Only 50mg caffeine per capsule, below the 75mg low end of our caffeine range
L-tyrosine (250mg) sits below the 300-500mg range
Not on the Australian Register of Therapeutic Goods (ARTG); imported as a food supplement
No published trial of Caffeine 2 itself; the evidence is for its ingredients
Small Trustpilot sample: 14 reviews for performancelab.com (3.8/5, checked 2026-10-05)
30-day money-back guarantee covers the first order only: one container, used up, with the claim filed within 60 days of delivery, refund minus shipping

name: Pre Lab Pro
summary: A low-caffeine pre-workout drink powder from Performance Lab. One 13g scoop gives 80mg natural caffeine, 160mg L-theanine and 400mg L-tyrosine, all within the ranges in our dosing audit, plus a 2,200mg Setria for Sport blend (L-citrulline and glutathione, split not disclosed) and 1,500mg red beet powder that are unlikely to reach the doses used in performance trials. Australian orders ship from the brand's Australian or UK depot (per performancelab.com's shipping page, checked 2026-10-05); it is imported as a food supplement, not a listed medicine.
whatItIs: Pre Lab Pro is a natural-berry-flavoured pre-workout powder sold through performancelab.com; the buy buttons on its own site, prelabpro.com, link to that product page. A tub holds 20 servings of one 13g scoop, mixed into 300ml of water and taken 15-30 minutes before training, with no more than 2 scoops in 24 hours. Each scoop also supplies 500mg Himalayan pink salt, vitamin D3 from algae, B2, B6, folate, B12, potassium and iron. It is vegan. For drug-tested athletes, the vendor states it is 'third-party tested and validated by Informed Sport', but the product page shows no certificate or batch number, so treat that as the vendor's claim. We found no entry for it on the Australian Register of Therapeutic Goods (ARTG) when we searched on 2026-10-05, so it reaches Australian buyers as an imported food supplement rather than a listed medicine.
howItWorks: Caffeine (80mg) blocks adenosine receptors to dull fatigue signals, and L-theanine (160mg, a 2:1 ratio) plus L-tyrosine (400mg) are the nootropic trio from Performance Lab's Caffeine 2 capsule at higher amounts. L-citrulline is converted to arginine and then nitric oxide, and beetroot supplies dietary nitrate, a second nitric-oxide source; the vendor includes both for blood flow, strength and endurance. Glutathione, an antioxidant, makes up the rest of the Setria for Sport blend. Himalayan pink salt (200mg sodium) and potassium act as electrolytes. Pre Lab Pro itself has not been tested in a published trial; the vendor's claims rest on ingredient-level research.
whatToExpect: Performance Lab says Pre Lab Pro starts working in around 15-30 minutes. The vendor calls the 80mg caffeine dose moderate, and two scoops (its 24-hour limit) give 160mg; count it toward your daily caffeine total. The citrulline and beet amounts are below the doses used in performance trials, so any blood-flow or endurance benefit from them is uncertain. Orders to Australia ship from the brand's Australian depot in 3-6 working days or from its UK depot in 7-14 working days, depending on destination (per performancelab.com's shipping page, checked 2026-10-05). We saw only US-dollar prices ($59 one-time for 20 scoops) when we checked.
pros: Caffeine, L-theanine and L-tyrosine all within our dosing-audit ranges
Vendor states Informed Sport testing, relevant to drug-tested athletes
Ships from an Australian depot (3-6 working days) or the UK (7-14)
Vegan, naturally flavoured powder with electrolytes
cons: Only 20 scoops per tub ($2.95 a serving at the $59 one-time price); the vendor's monthly plan delivers one tub, so a scoop every day would need more than one tub a month
Setria for Sport blend (2,200mg) does not split L-citrulline and glutathione; even if it were all citrulline it would sit below the roughly 3g low end of citrulline trials
1.5g red beet powder with no stated nitrate content, very likely far below the roughly 6-8 mmol of nitrate used in beetroot trials
Several verified reviews on prelabpro.com report powder that set rock-hard in the tub; the company replied it had 'a bad batch' that was 'taken off sale' (checked 2026-10-05)

Strict 30-day guarantee: first order only, one tub, used up before claiming, refund minus shipping; performancelab.com allows claims within 60 days of delivery, but prelabpro.com's returns page says 30 days, so confirm the terms first
Not on the Australian Register of Therapeutic Goods (ARTG); imported as a food supplement
No published trial of Pre Lab Pro itself; the evidence is for its ingredients
